case_name: Punjab Water Supply & Sewerage Board v Ranjodh Singh and Others
facts: The appeals involve the question of applicability of a purported policy decision of the State as regards regularization of services of the employees of Appellant-Board.

It is a local authority that undertakes execution of schemes of various nature including laying down of sewerage lines, water supply etc. for Municipalities, Municipal Corporations and Improvement Trusts.

Respondents in these appeals were engaged on contract basis in two different schemes, i.e., for maintenance of water supply and sewerage lines for Municipal Corporation, Ludhiana and for maintenance of tube wells installed under URP project for Municipal Corporation, Hoshiarpur respectively.

Their services were terminated. Respondents prayed for regularization of the services. The said prayer was rejected by the appellant in terms of the scheme framed scheme for regularization by the State of Punjab on 23.1.2001 and 28.3.2003.
issues: What is the applicability of a purported policy decision of the State as regards regularization of services of the employees of Appellant-Board?
Can the statutory bodies refuse to fulfill their constitutional duty to implement the scheme of equality?
petitioner_arguments: The purported scheme of State of Punjab cannot be said to be applicable to the employees of the appellant-board.
A circular letter is not a statutory instrument.
The statutory bodies are bound to apply the rules of recruitment laid down under statutory rules.
respondent_arguments: The workmen had been working for years and many of them had already crossed the age fixed for entry to the Government service, as such they are entitled to regularization.
No person illegally appointed or appointed without following the procedure prescribed under the law, is entitled to claim that he should be continued in service.
court_reasoning: The State may have some control with regard to recruitment of employees of local authorities, but such control must be exercised by the State strictly in terms of the provisions of the Act.
The statutory bodies are bound to apply the rules of recruitment laid down under statutory rules.
No regularization is permissible in exercise of the statutory power conferred u/art. 162 of the Constitution if the appointments have been made in contravention of the statutory rules.
holding: The High Court allowed the writ petitions directing the appellant to reinstate the respondents in service with all consequential benefits and to regularize their services.
The impugned judgment is set aside and the appeals are allowed.
